claim_verdicts.evidence: time-zone-overview.md: "The time in any of the world's time zones can be expressed as an offset from Coordinated Universal Time (UTC)." custom-date-and-time-format-strings.md ('zzz'): "A plus sign (+) indicates hours ahead of UTC". let-users-resolve-ambiguous-times.md: "Get the UTC date and time by subtracting the offset ... from the local time." datetime/index.md: a DateTimeOffset value "unambiguously identifies a single point in time." time-demo: 06:20+07:00 -> 23:20+00:00.

standard-date-and-time-format-strings.md: 'o' emits a string that "complies with ISO 8601"; for DateTimeOffset the pattern is "yyyy'-'MM'-'dd'T'HH':'mm':'ss'.'fffffffzzz"; of "the three ways that ISO 8601 represents time zone information", "DateTimeKind.Unspecified date and time values have no time zone information." PG 17 §8.5.2: "ISO 8601 specifies the use of uppercase letter T to separate the date and time."

PG 17 §8.5.1.3: "For timestamp with time zone values, an input string that includes an explicit time zone will be converted to UTC ... using the appropriate offset for that time zone." "In either case, the value is stored internally as UTC, and the originally stated or assumed time zone is not retained." Lab: '2026-03-31T06:20:00+07:00'::timestamptz = '2026-03-30T23:20:00+00:00'::timestamptz -> t.

Arithmetic on seed times at +07: order 6 05:30 -> 22:30 UTC previous day; 12 06:20 -> 23:20 previous day; 7 07:45 -> 00:45 same day; 3 08:05 -> 01:05 same day. The file's second query (UTC date <> Vietnam date), run in the lab, returns exactly ids 6 and 12.

claim_verdicts.evidence: converting-between-time-zones.md: "The use of UTC is recommended when a date and time's portability across computers is important." §4 keeps the condition ("When a moment is read by more than one program or machine"). Npgsql docs (key npgsql; lab pins 9.0.4): "Npgsql maps UTC DateTime to timestamp with time zone ... trying to send a non-UTC DateTime as timestamptz will throw", so UtcNow into timestamptz (§6) is what the lab's driver expects.

PG 17 §8.5.1.3: "In a value that has been determined to be timestamp without time zone, PostgreSQL will silently ignore any time zone indication. That is, the resulting value is derived from the date/time fields in the input string, and is not adjusted for time zone." Lab: `'2026-03-31T06:20:00+07:00'::timestamp` -> `2026-03-31 06:20:00` (offset dropped, digits kept).

time-zone-overview.md: Invalid time: "A nonexistent time ... It occurs when the clock time is adjusted forward in time"; Ambiguous time: "A time that can be mapped to two different times in a single time zone. It occurs when the clock time is adjusted back in time"; Fixed rule: "An adjustment rule that sets a particular date for the transition to or from daylight saving time."

globalization-icu.md: "ICU provides the flexibility to create TimeZoneInfo instances using IANA time zone IDs, even when the application is running on Windows" but "this functionality isn't available when using NLS mode or globalization invariant mode". dotnet-6.md: IANA or Windows ids "on any operating system that has time zone data installed". csproj@stage-0: `<InvariantGlobalization>false`. time-demo resolved the id on the Windows 10 host.

PG 17 §9.9.4: "timestamp with time zone AT TIME ZONE zone → timestamp without time zone ... Converts given time stamp with time zone to time stamp without time zone, as the time would appear in that zone." Lab: pg_typeof(now() AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') = `timestamp without time zone`; date(...) columns show `2026-03-30`, `2026-03-31`.

issues.quote: "Vietnam has no time zone problems because it has no daylight saving."

It first appears inside the belief I am supposed to have held, and is explained only afterwards in one dense sentence ('forward, and some local times never happen; back, and some happen twice'). Without the term I could not have held this belief. Summary line 5 and option b of q1-q4 also lean on it.
issues.fix: Move the sentence 'A zone with daylight saving moves its clocks on set dates…' into the time zone bullet of Core concepts, phrased as: some zones move their clocks forward and back on set dates each year (daylight saving); Vietnam's does not.
